title: Microsoft Teams: explicit recording and transcription consent for PSTN participants in GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates the compliance assurance by saying recordings can carry an explicit choice from every participant. Microsoft documents participants who are automatically consented without interaction; the controls and roadmap details otherwise check out, with smaller documentation and licensing qualifications needed.

claims.claim: The change extends explicit recording and transcription consent to PSTN participants in Teams meetings in GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: We are introducing explicit recording and transcription consent support for PSTN participants joining Microsoft Teams meetings in GCC High and DoD environments.

claims.quote: This feature is already available in Public and GCC clouds and is now being extended to sovereign environments.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Who is affected
claims.claim: The roadmap says PSTN participants are prompted for consent before unmuting when a meeting is recorded or transcribed.
claims.quote: After this rollout, when a meeting is being recorded or transcribed, PSTN participants will be prompted to provide explicit consent before they can unmute and participate.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: PSTN participants who do not provide consent remain muted for the meeting.
claims.quote: If consent is not provided, participants will remain muted for the duration of the meeting.

claims.where: Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Teams clients already have an explicit consent experience.
claims.quote: This update aligns PSTN behavior with the existing consent experience in Teams clients

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends informing users about the change so they are prepared to consent.
claims.quote: We recommend informing users about this change so they are prepared to provide consent when prompted.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap description does not specify a consent policy setting.
claims.quote: After this rollout, when a meeting is being recorded or transcribed, PSTN participants will be prompted to provide explicit consent before they can unmute and participate.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Audio Conferencing callers press 1 to consent and unmute.
claims.quote: 1 - Give consent to being recorded and transcribed in a call and un-mute their microphone.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Audio Conferencing callers press 2 to decline consent and remain muted.
claims.quote: 2 – Deny recording and transcription, and remain muted.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Callers who previously declined can press *6 to unmute and are prompted for consent before speaking.
claims.quote: If the user previously declined consent but later wants to unmute and speak, they can press \***6** to unmute. They are prompted to provide consent before they can speak.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: If a policy mutes all participants on joining, callers must press *5 to raise a hand before providing consent again.
claims.quote: If you use a policy to mute all participants upon joining a meeting, participants must press \*5 to raise hand before providing consent again.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Platforms
claims.claim: Explicit consent supports Audio Conferencing dial-in participants and PSTN endpoints in meetings and group calls.
claims.quote:
Explicit consent is supported on the following endpoints:
- Mobile Teams (Android and iOS)
- Meeting participants dialing in using Audio Conferencing
- PSTN endpoints in meetings and group calls

claims.where: Scope: Platforms
claims.claim: Supported explicit-consent endpoints include Mobile Teams on Android and iOS, native Mac and Windows, and Teams Web.
claims.quote:
Mobile Teams (Android and iOS)
Teams native Mac
Teams native Windows
Teams Web

claims.where: Scope: Platforms
claims.claim: Explicit consent is unsupported on CarPlay, old native clients and Teams Displays.
claims.quote:
Explicit consent isn’t supported on the following endpoints, along with any endpoints not listed under supported endpoints:
- CarPlay
- Old version native clients
- Teams Displays

claims.where: Scope: Platforms
claims.claim: Users on unsupported endpoints have a view-only experience in meetings requiring explicit consent.
claims.quote: In meetings requiring explicit consent, users joining from unsupported endpoints have the view-only experience.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Learn documents the consent control as Off (Disabled) by default and enabled by an administrator, corresponding to admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: | Off | Disabled | This setting is the default value. For organizers with this policy, participants aren't asked for consent to be recorded and transcribed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: With the policy Off, participants are not asked for consent and are included in recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: For organizers with this policy, participants aren't asked for consent to be recorded and transcribed. All participants are included in recordings and transcripts from these organizers' meetings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & Transcription > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription manages consent, including Audio Conferencing.
claims.quote: Under Meetings, select Meeting Policies. ... Within your chosen policy, navigate to the Recording & Transcription section. Toggle the Require participant agreement for recording and transcription setting On or Off.
claims.fix: Keep the documented path, but add to controls[0].note: 'The participant agreement page documents Teams admin center management; the Audio Conferencing page says PowerShell must be used for Audio Conferencing consent.' Both pages are already cited: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/participant-agreement-recording-transcription and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/conferencing-recording-consent.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent Enabled requires consent for meetings created by organizers with that policy.
claims.quote:
To require participants to give their explicit consent to be recorded or transcribed in any meeting that organizers with this policy create, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent Enabled

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Scope: Who is affected; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The consent meeting policy applies to meetings created by organizers assigned that policy, and requires consent when On.
claims.quote: | On | Enabled | For organizers with this policy, all their meetings require participants to provide consent to be recorded and transcribed. |

claims.where: Scope: Who is affected
claims.claim: The consent policy also applies to channel meetings.
claims.quote: This policy also applies to channel meetings.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The meeting policy ExplicitRecordingConsent parameter also controls consent for Audio Conferencing.
claims.quote: The -ExplicitRecordingConsent parameter also controls recording consent for Audio Conferencing.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecording $true allows recording for users governed by the Global meeting policy.

To allow everyone in your organization to record, except users with an assigned custom meeting policy, run the following command:

claims.where: controls[1].governs, scope and note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing meeting recording control allows or prevents users recording meetings rather than configuring participant consent.
claims.quote: Determines whether cloud recording is allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow the user to be able to record meetings. Set this to FALSE to prohibit the user from recording meetings.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Administrators can use Global or custom meeting policies and assign a policy to users or groups.
claims.quote: To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the Global policy. To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Recordings and transcripts of these meetings can carry an explicit choice from every participant.
claims.quote: The following user types are auto consented for recording and transcription without any participant interaction. They get a consent notification, and their consent data is logged as 'not applicable' or 'auto consent':
claims.fix: Replace 'Recordings and transcripts of those meetings can then carry an explicit choice from every participant' with 'PSTN dial-in participants can provide explicit consent before speaking.' The cited participant agreement page documents auto-consented participants, so do not promise an explicit choice from everyone.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Consent choices appear in the attendance report.
claims.quote: The consent choice for each participant is included in the attendance report. ... When the attendance report is disabled or participants aren't in the attendance report, organizers and co-organizers don't see consent data.
claims.fix: Qualify the first attendance-report statement with: 'When the attendance report is disabled or participants are excluded, organizers and co-organizers do not see that consent data; admins can still see it in audit logs.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/participant-agreement-recording-transcription.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can see meeting consent data in Purview Teams meeting audit logs.
claims.quote: The second is with the Added information about meeting participants filter in the Teams meeting audit logs in Purview. Consent data is in the audit logs regardless of your policy that manages the attendance and engagement report or your users' option for tracking attendance.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: No change to authentication or access is described for this consent extension.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams explicit recording transcription consent authentication access changes PSTN participants'; read the roadmap and participant-agreement-recording-transcription, conferencing-recording-consent and call-recording-transcription-captions. No authentication or admission change is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Teams client participants who decline consent have a view-only experience.
claims.quote: If a participant responds 'No' to the question, they have a view-only meeting experience.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: View-only participants cannot start recording or transcription in meetings requiring explicit consent.
claims.quote: View-only participants can't start recording or transcription for any meetings that require explicit consent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The participant agreement page lists PSTN endpoints in 1:1 calls as auto-consented endpoints.
claims.quote:
Auto consent endpoints and platforms
The following user types are auto consented for recording and transcription without any participant interaction. ... PSTN endpoints in 1:1 calls
claims.fix: Replace the security bullet's second sentence with: 'The participant agreement page lists PSTN endpoints in 1:1 calls as auto-consented, while the call recording page documents explicit consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls under the Calling policy.' Both pages are already cited; remove 'in meetings' and the inferred 'so'.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN call consent uses the separate Teams Calling policy, while Audio Conferencing and group calls use the meeting policy.
claims.quote: This parameter manages recording consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls. Audio conferencing and group calls are managed by Teams Meeting Policy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence statement specific to this consent feature is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' under the standard's rule for an option inside a licensed product. State: 'This is a consent option inside licensed Microsoft Teams. Except for joining meetings anonymously, organizational users need a Teams license. No licence or meter specific to this consent extension was found as of November 2026.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/user-access and use that narrower gap in Cost and licensing, Open questions and the cost rationale; do not imply all product licensing is unpublished.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The explicit consent pages and roadmap name no licence, meter or charge specifically for explicit recording consent.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams explicit recording transcription consent licensing Teams Premium Audio Conferencing license'; opened both consent pages, meeting-recording, user-access and Teams add-on licensing; read roadmap. No consent-specific licence, meter or charge found.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: No separate admin switch for the PSTN prompt is documented in the pages read as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams explicit recording consent PSTN separate admin setting PowerShell ExplicitRecordingConsent audio conferencing'; read both consent pages, meeting-recording and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy consent parameters. Only the shared meeting consent parameter is documented for Audio Conferencing.
